original.description: Objective: To develop innovative end-to-end payload system architectures, techniques and algorithms enabling large distributed arrays for PNT based on high-gain beamforming.Description: Large arrays of antennas and distributed arrays of antennas are being considered for the generation of very high-gain beamforming. In this case, the main objective is to achieve a high received power by the ground user receivers, such that high data rates can be supported per user. Large and distributed arrays can be considered for PNT, both for Earth and Spaced Service Volume users and applications. One clear expected advantage would be to achieve much larger received power on the user receivers than with current GNSS systems. This can be of interest in particular in harsh propagation conditions, including the presence of interference and jamming, or to reach very far-away space users/assets. The objective of this activity is to design techniques and algorithms to enable large distributed array satellite and payload (PL) system architectures/configurations for PNT. The focus will be on the generation of very high-gain beamforming, while ensuring the transmission of high-accuracy signals-in-space, even when wide-band signals are used. Both the transmission in L-band (reference) and alternative bands (e.g., S and Cbands) will be addressed. Additionally, the activity will investigate innovative ideas for the exploitation of the large distributedarray architecture for PNT purposes, leveraging concepts and operational modes exploited in other space applications like SyntheticAperture Radar (SAR) systems. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Definition and design of innovative techniques and algorithms in the areas identified above; - Implementation of the required tools/software enabling the assessment of the proposed techniques and algorithms; - Assessment/test of the different techniques and algorithms in simulated conditions; - Identification of themost promising techniques/algorithms based on the results obtained; - Definition of the proposed the way-forward to further matureeach of the promising techniques/algorithms identified.Deliverables: Report, SoftwareProcurement Policy: C(2) = Activities in open competition, where a significant participation of non-LSI is requested. original.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop, manufacture and test an Ethernet switch/router Intellectual Property (IP)core and test chip supporting layers 1 to 3 packet processing for constellations. The IP core shall be developed, implemented on a test chip using the optimal UDSM ASIC technology node(s) selected as part of this activity to achieve the desired performance, and tested using a validation breadboard.Targeted Improvements: Enabling a European or Canadian source of terabit class ethernet switch/routers for multi-orbit constellation applications.Description: Cost sensitive, high volume multi-orbit constellation solutions require a tailored ethernet packet switch/router adapted to high data rates (at and above 100 Gbps), number of ports (16 and more) and supported protocols. An ethernet switch/router, scalable in data rate and number of ports and supporting layer 1 to 3 protocols, is not available from a European or Canadian supplier. Existing commercial solutions cannot be readily adapted to the needs of satcom applications in low earth orbit and multi-orbit constellations.This activity will be implemented in a phased approach. In Phase 1, an ethernet switch/router IP core shall be developed utilising ultra-deep sub-micron (UDSM) ASIC technology (targeting 7nm or below) to achieve 1 terabit per second data throughput for low earth orbit and multi-orbit constellation applications. The data rateper port and number of ports forming a channel shall be configurable to suit multiple applications (configurable number of ports from 4 to at least 16 ports, with configurable port data rate from 1Gbps to at least100Gbps per port). Multi-protocol label switchingand the internet protocol shall be supported. Phase 1 will conclude with the completed IP core design, verified and synthesised in the design environment, to generate the ASIC test chip tape-out files ready for fabrication. The budget for Phase 1 is up to 2,000 kEuro.In the second phase, the IP core will be implemented in the selected UDSM ASIC technology as an ASIC test-chip (via a Multi Project Wafer Run or shared Full Mask Run). A validation breadboard shall be designed and built to undertake performance testing of thetest chip. The test chip shall be representative of a scaled version of a final product and shall be tested in relevant environment.IP cores developed in this activity shall be available for further development by ESA Member State and Canadian industries at fair and reasonable market conditions.

While it is made visible to all ESA Member States, Associate Members and European Cooperating States, this CfP will be addressed only to Slovenian legal entities registered in ESA-STAR, as prime tenderer and foresees the following standard activity types:Type A Research and Preparatory Activities, aimed at the preparation for participation in ESA optional programmes or the initial steps of a product development for Space, with potential for use on futureESA missions or commercial missions. The start TRL shall be at least 1 and the target TRL shall be TRL 3 or below. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 150,000.Type B Flight- and Ground Segment-related Research and Development Activities, targetting equipment to build competences and capabilities centred on products or generic technology development with potential for re-use on ESA or commercial missions. The start TRL shall be at least 3 and the target TRL shall be TRL 5. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 400 000 (flight related)/EUR 300 000 (ground related).Type C Flight Opportunities for mature existing Slovenian technologies or products in collaboration with experienced European players, to be involved in non-ESA mission in order to become flight proven. The start TRL shall be at least 5 and the target TRL shall be TRL 9. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 750 000 (inc. launch and operation cost). The work carried out by the Tenderer must be co-funded to a minimum level of 25% of the total cost of the activity. Maximum 20% of the budget may be assigned tonon-Slovenian entities, however launch and integration tasks are excluded from this limitation.Type D Space science activities, supporting the involvement of national researchers leading to potential of future involvement in ESA science mission core team and publication of peer reviewed scientific papers. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 100,000.Type F Space Applications, products and services making use of ESA/ European space infrastructure that is already existing or scheduled for operation in the near term. The start TRLshall be at least 6 and the target TRL shall be TRL 8. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 200,000. The work carried out by the Tenderer must be co-funded to a minimum level of 25% of the total cost of the activity.Type G1 University courses/modules leading to a qualification (BSc or MSc) in space related topics that correspond to the needs of national space industry and to encourage career in spaceandanswer to national space industry needs. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 70,000.To be published as a separate tender in esa-star: TypeG2 PhD Theses that correspond to a clear need from the national space industry and would lead to a new product or service beingableto be developed. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 70,000 with a minimum company co-funding of EUR 10,000. To be published in the Open Space Innovation Platform (OSIP, https://ideas.esa.int/): Type H  Space Related Training Courses, for the cost reimbursement of participation of employees in space related training courses. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 9,999. More information and further programmatic constraints can be consulted in the cover letter of the call upon its issue date.
